source.title: Implicit bias of SGD in L2-regularized linear DNNs: One-way jumps from high to low rank

record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendix supplied
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own theoretical and empirical results on how SGD and training conditions affect rank and test loss in deep linear matrix-completion networks, a related but distinct setting from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Results on rank jumps and matrix-completion test loss bear on the claim's generalization subject, but none measures the natural-label generalization behavior or the specific properties named in V1–V8. Empirical figures compare training schedules and depth; cited optimizer/generalization findings are prior work and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study establishes low-rank bias and reports matrix-completion test loss in L2-regularized deep linear networks. These results measure none of V1–V8. Learning-rate and ridge schedules do not test batch-size effects, and SGD versus near-GD behavior does not test adaptive optimizers versus SGD.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: L2-regularized deep linear networks have minima of different ranks, and SGD can make one-way transitions toward lower-rank regions under stated conditions; experiments observe such jumps. The formal result concerns absorbing approximate-rank regions, requires suitable parameters and independent sampling with replacement, and can imply extremely long waiting times. Indefinitely continuing training can underestimate the desired rank, so lower rank does not guarantee better generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses L2-regularized deep linear networks trained by SGD on matrix-completion tasks; it does not test the natural-label image or language classification recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Jump behavior changes with depth, task difficulty ϵ, and learning-rate/ridge schedule; larger depth and high-noise periods are reported to make jumps more likely.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the theorem's parameter and sampling conditions, approximate low-rank regions are absorbing, and SGD eventually reaches them; this concerns rank dynamics rather than any listed generalization effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD with L2 regularization has a one-way bias toward lower-rank regions in deep linear matrix-completion networks.

fits_no_version.finding: On the studied 2 × 2 matrix-completion tasks, staged or periodic learning-rate and ridge schedules enable rank-reducing jumps and subsequent recovery of the missing entry. Greater depth and longer high-noise phases facilitate these jumps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth and training schedules affect low-rank recovery and held-out matrix-completion loss in the studied deep linear networks.

record.problems: Empirical evidence is limited to small 2 × 2 matrix-completion problems and figure-based test-loss plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The theory assumes independent sampling with replacement, while the authors note practical shuffled epochs may prevent the predicted jumps within an epoch; expected jump times can be extremely large.
record.rows_left_out: No separate result rows were omitted. The theoretical theorem gives probability and rank claims but no reported test-error measurement; cited prior-work findings were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, weight-decay changes, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps and its ranking against other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites large-batch generalization work as motivation but supplies no batch-size experiment. Its own related results do not justify the record's tests/T2 classification. States of cannot_determine indicate that the rows cannot establish a listed version, not that their qualitative rank-recovery findings are unreadable.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label accuracy.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization on image or language benchmarks.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and measured generalization gap.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: DLN with L = 3, w1 = 100
rows.operation_detail: SGD annealing schedule on 2 × 2 matrix-completion task; test loss over time

conditions.value: η = 0.03 for first 500 steps, then η = 0.25 until t = 5000, then η = 0.05 and λ = 0.001

rows.measure: test loss and second-to-first singular-value ratio over time
rows.note: Figure description states a jump around time 2000 where the output becomes rank 1; test loss values are not given in text.
rows.check: The schedule is incorrect: Figure 1 uses η = 0.03 for the first 500 steps, then η = 0.2 with λ = 0.1. Offshoots created at different times use η = 0.02 and λ = 0.001; there is no stated switch at t = 5000. The caption reports a rank-1 jump around t = 2000; offshoots after it recover the missing entry, whereas earlier offshoots fail. Neither measure tests a listed version.

rows.subject: DLNs with L = 3 and L = 4
rows.operation_detail: SGD under the same staged learning-rate and ridge schedule; test loss over time

conditions.value: L = 3 or L = 4; five networks per depth

rows.measure: test loss and second-to-first singular-value ratio over time
rows.note: Text says none of the five L = 3 networks jumped in this time, while all five L = 4 networks jumped at different times during the first 5000 SGD steps; the plotted test-loss values are not stated.
rows.check: Figure 2 plots test loss, not a singular-value ratio. Its explicit result is zero of five depth-3 networks jumping versus five of five depth-4 networks within the first 5000 steps. The extracted partial state has no applicable claim version.

rows.subject: DLNs with L = 4, w = 100
rows.operation_detail: SGD annealing schedule; test loss relative to test loss from zero-filling the missing entry

conditions.value: 2 × 2 MC problem; range of ϵ values
t0 = 0, 250, 1000, or 4000 steps, followed by 4000 low-noise steps

rows.measure: test loss divided by test loss when putting zeros in the missing entries
rows.baseline: test loss when putting zeros in the missing entries
rows.note: Text says without a high-noise period the network fails to recover the rank 1 solution even for ϵ = 1; longer high-noise durations allow recovery for smaller ϵ. Numerical plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The qualitative schedule effect is stated clearly: no high-noise phase fails to recover rank 1 even at ϵ = 1, while longer phases permit recovery at smaller ϵ. This does not measure any listed version, so partial is inapplicable.

rows.subject: DLN with L = 3, w1 = 100
rows.operation_detail: SGD with periodic alternation between large and small learning-rate and ridge settings

conditions.value: alternating η = 0.1, λ = 0.001 and η = 0.4, λ = 0.1

rows.note: Text says jumps occur during large η, λ periods and SGD can jump again in a subsequent large η, λ period after settling near a minimum; plotted test-loss values are not stated.
rows.check: The caption and discussion report jumps during high-learning-rate, high-ridge periods and low test error during subsequent slow periods. This schedule effect does not measure any listed version, so partial is inapplicable.
